Program Information
The Department of Environmental Engineering Sciences offers the degrees of Master of Science (thesis or non-thesis), Master of Engineering (thesis or non-thesis), and Doctor of Philosophy in Environmental Engineering Sciences. Official minimum requirements for these degrees are given in the Graduate Degrees section of this catalog. The descriptions below supplement these minimum requirements.
Master of Science & Master of Engineering
Any Master’s degree candidate may pursue the Master of Science degree (M.S.); only those holding ABET-accredited baccalaureate degrees in engineering may choose the Master of Engineering degree (M.E.). All other degree requirements remain the same. A non-thesis Master’s degree candidate must establish a Plan of Study that has been approved by their advisor by the end of the first term of enrollment. A Master’s degree candidate seeking a thesis option must form a supervisory committee and establish a Plan of Study that has been approved by their advisor by the midpoint of the second term of enrollment. As the candidate progresses toward their degree, any deviations in their program from an approved Plan of Study should be recorded by the submission of a revised Plan of Study.
A total of 30 credit hours is required for the Master’s degree. Of this total, for non-thesis students, at least 15 credits of coursework must be in the student’s major field of study. For thesis students, at least 12 credits of coursework must be in the student’s major field of study. Technical courses from other fields may be used to satisfy the remaining credits, provided they are graduate-level courses (5000 and above). All Master’s students are required to take 1 credit of the general environmental engineering section of ENV6935, Graduate Environmental Engineering Seminar. Other sections with the same course number (e.g., Wetland Seminar, Air Workshop) do not satisfy this requirement.
The Master’s degree with thesis option includes a minimum of 24 graded credit hours of coursework and up to 6 credit hours of ENV6971 Research for Master’s Thesis. Thesis students must have at least one article submitted to a peer-reviewed journal prior to graduation.
For both the thesis and non-thesis degrees, up to 6 credit hours of out-of-department coursework at the 3000 or 4000 level may be completed to satisfy degree requirements, as long as the coursework completed is included in an approved Plan of Study.
A comprehensive final examination is required by the Graduate School for a Master’s student taking the non-thesis option. The exam will take place during the final semester of the program. Students will be notified by email regarding the exam.
Doctor of Philosophy
The Doctor of Philosophy (Ph.D.) is a research-intensive degree requiring independent mastery of a field of knowledge. As such, considerable flexibility is allowed by the Graduate School and the department in tailoring individual programs.
All Ph.D. students must take a minimum of 12 graded credit hours in the major. Work in the major must be in courses numbered 5000 or above. For work outside the major, 6 credits of courses numbered 3000 or above may be taken if part of an approved plan of study. All Ph.D. students are required to take 1 credit of the general environmental engineering section of ENV6935, Graduate Environmental Engineering Seminar. Other sections with the same course number (e.g., Wetland Seminar, Air Workshop) do not satisfy this requirement. Ph.D. students must have at least one article accepted in a peer-reviewed journal prior to graduation.
Students must form a Ph.D. supervisory committee and must complete a Plan of Study approved by their advisor by the midpoint of the third term of enrollment. As the student progresses toward the degree, any significant deviations from the approved Plan of Study should be discussed and approved by the student’s advisor and recorded in the submission of a revised Plan of Study.
Direct admission into the Master of Science and Doctor of Philosophy programs requires a bachelor’s degree in engineering or in a basic science such as chemistry, geology, physics, biology, or mathematics. Persons with a degree in a nontechnical field may also be admitted into this program after completing appropriate technical courses. Direct admission into the Master of Engineering program requires a bachelor’s degree in engineering from an ABET-accredited institution. Requirements for a master’s degree normally take 12 to 24 months to complete. The length of time required for the Doctor of Philosophy degree depends partly on the research topic and may be completed in three years, but it is often longer, depending on prior academic experience.
Combination degree programs: The department offers a combination bachelor’s/master’s degree program. This program allows qualified students to earn both a bachelor’s degree and a master’s degree, with a savings of 12 credits. In addition, the Environmental Engineering Sciences Department, in partnership with the Levin College of Law, offers a combination professional/graduate program leading to the M.S. or M.E. degree in environmental engineering sciences and the Juris Doctor degree. Twelve credits of appropriate coursework are counted toward both degrees. Please see the academic units for guidance.
For more information, please visit our website at http://www.essie.ufl.edu.
